exact_statement: There exists a universal C such that every Boolean f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} under uniform measure satisfies H(hat_f^2) <= C I(f), where H=sum_S hat_f(S)^2 log_2(1/hat_f(S)^2), I=sum_S |S|hat_f(S)^2, and 0 log(1/0)=0.
assumptions: Boolean-valued f, finite n, uniform product measure, Walsh normalization
source: O'Donnell-Wright-Zhou, The Fourier Entropy-Influence Conjecture for certain classes of Boolean functions, https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/fei.pdf, p.2; attributes conjecture to Friedgut-Kalai 1996
source_quote: Fourier Entropy–Influence (FEI) Conjecture. ∃C ∀f, H[ f̂²] ≤ C · I[f].
remaining_gap: General Boolean functions; no dimension-free entropy bound verified

exact_statement: For arbitrary probability laws p on subsets of [n], H(p) <= C E_p|S| cannot hold for a universal C: the uniform law on n singleton sets has H=log_2 n and E|S|=1.
assumptions: n>=2, no Boolean Fourier realizability requirement
source_quote: Discarding the Boolean constraint destroys the claim: the probability measure uniform on the n singleton subse
proof_or_counterexample: Set p({i})=1/n. Then H(p)=sum_i (1/n)log_2 n=log_2 n, while E_p|S|=1.
remaining_gap: This rejects a relaxation, not FEI for Boolean functions.
